title: Context-aware soft admission using credit-slope and fidelity modes
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: During cross-region surges we need a predictable, tenant-fair mechanism to preserve SLOs without hard-denying traffic. Existing admission heuristics are either too coarse (global circuit breakers) or too brittle (hard thresholds).

Goal: Implement a context-aware soft-admission controller that uses a per-tenant credit-slope (time-decayed credits) combined with a small set of graceful fidelity degradation modes. The controller should preserve latency SLOs for high-priority routes, provide predictable fairness across tenants, and enable safe multi-region failover by allowing controlled capacity spillovers.

Solution overview:
- Credit-slope: each tenant has a credit bucket that replenishes at a rate determined by their tier and recent consumption. Credits decay over time (slope) rather than discrete refill windows, enabling smoother behavior on bursty workloads.
- Probabilistic admission: request admission probability p = min(1, credits / cost_estimate). This allows soft rejections (probabilistic shed) during contention instead of abrupt denials.
- Fidelity modes: three ranked modes per route: full (no change), slim (token-aware trimming: reduce max tokens, disable streaming partials), summary-only (short extraction/condensed response). Routes are mapped to a fidelity ladder; admission controller may downgrade mode for accepted requests when credits low to preserve latency SLOs.
- Context signals: admission uses token-estimate, historical latency/quantile windows, region capacity headroom, and contract tier. It prefers degrading fidelity for lower-cost savings before denying requests from premium tenants.

Implementation plan:
1) Shim on non-blocking admission path: introduce a CreditProvider interface implemented by an in-process cache backed by regional Redis for quick refills and periodic reconciliation to the central state.
2) Admission algorithm: evaluate route metadata, cost_estimate (tokens*decode_cost_coefficient), tenant_credits, and region_headroom. Compute p and decide admitted/reject/forced-degrade.
3) Fidelity enforcement: on accept with downgrade, attach response hints to runtime to enforce trimming at decode time. Add tracing fields for mode and credit usage.
4) Telemetry: add per-tenant credit level, admission decisions, reject_rate, downgrade_rate, p50/p95 latency by mode and region. Expose dashboards and alerts for deviation from SLO budgets.
5) Gradual rollout: dark-launch decision logs -> canary in non-critical region -> 50% traffic with only downgrade allowed -> enable probabilistic shedding -> enable cross-region spillover logic.

Trade-offs & considerations:
- Redis-backed credits favor speed but introduce cross-region staleness; mitigation: local fast-cache with conservative reads and periodic reconciliation.
- Probabilistic admission can create variance for small tenants; address by floor guarantees (minimum admission rate based on contract).
- Fidelity downgrades risk user experience drift; must be gated by evals and customer opt-outs on critical routes.

Success criteria:
- 99.9% of P99 latency SLOs preserved for premium routes during simulated 3x traffic spikes in staging.
- Reduction in hard rejections (HTTP 429) by >= 60% compared to current threshold-based policy under the same load profile.
- Clear per-tenant cost telemetry enabling ops to correlate credits consumption and billing anomalies.

Runbook (short):
- Operator sees rising downgrade_rate + total_admission_drop in Dashboard A -> check region_headroom and credit-pool drain.
- If cross-region spillover misbehaves, revert probabilistic shedding feature flag for affected region and restore previous admission policy.
- For tenant-specific incidents, temporarily top-up credits via admin API and investigate workload pattern.

Rollout checklist:
- Design doc approved (Confluence)
- Unit and e2e tests for credit math and downgrade enforcement
- Telemetry dashboard and alerts in place
- Feature flag with staged rollout pipeline

Notes: coordinate with console team to surface tenant credit balances for SEs and with billing to ensure credit policies map to contracts.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Kenji Sato: Initial spike-proof prototype in branch feature/credit-slope exists. Benchmarks show <3ms per-decision overhead with local cache. Opening PR next week.

2025-02-14 - Maya Patel (PM): +1 on prioritizing premium-route protection. Please add a minimum admission floor for Enterprise tenants; we cannot probabilistically drop their traffic below 95% acceptance.
2025-02-20 - Kenji Sato: Implemented admission floor for tiers; added config 'min_accept_rate' per contract. Updated unit tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1426
2025-02-25 - Security (Liam O'Connor): Read through design; no KMS impact; ensure audit logs include credit adjustments. Marked security_review_required=false but flagged audit requirement.

2025-03-01 - QA (Rina Chen): Staging chaos test with regional outage simulated; downgrade-only mode prevented SLA breaches on majority of routes. Found edge-case where requests with incorrect token_estimate circumvent downgrade; filed follow-up ENG-688101.

2025-03-04 - Kenji Sato: Canary rollout started in eu-west-1 with 5% traffic; dashboards show expected drop in hard rejects and downgrade_rate at ~8%. Next: expand to us-central-1 at 20% if metrics stable for 72h.
